metadata.case_name: LAI CHI PON v. TOTO STEEL & IRON WORKS LTD AND OTHERS

injuries.description: He was found to have a compressed fracture of his vertebra at T11 and T12.
source: He was found to have a compressed fracture of his vertebra at T11 and T12.

injuries.description: The Plaintiff is now an incomplete paraplegic.
source: The Plaintiff is now an incomplete paraplegic.
injuries.icd_description: Other incomplete cord syndrome of lumbar spinal cord

manifestations.description: Limited movement of his lower limbs
He is unable to stand without support.
He can only walk with crutches and an ankle-foot orthosis.
He can only walk awkwardly and clumsily.
He cannot run or move or turn quickly.
He is not able to walk on any slopes and has great difficulties climbing stairs.
He cannot carry anything heavy when using crutches, other than a small light bag hanging from the crutches.
He is unable to sit for more than an hour, otherwise he will suffer unbearable pain in his back.
The crutches have caused blisters on his palms. His ankle-foot orthosis has also caused blisters on his feet. He needs ointment to clean the wounds on his feet.
Reduced sensation from his abdomen downwards
Generally the Plaintiff has no sensation below the knee. The sensation in his thighs is limited.
He gets constant pain, discomfort and paraesthesia in both legs, above the knees.
He is unable to feel temperatures.
When he is sleeping or sitting, he gets spasms in both legs. The spasms occur about 2-3 times per week... They will last for about 15 minutes.
Double Incontinence
He still suffers from bladder problems. He has partial bladder sensation with reflex emptying and a tendency to retention.
He empties his bladder by straining and tapping on the abdomen.
He still wets himself twice a week. He needs to wear diapers at night.
He moves his bowel every 2 to 3 days and requires suppositories.
He is still occasionally incontinent.
Sexual dysfunction
His sexual ability is greatly impaired.
He fails 70% of his attempts to have sexual intercourse with his wife which causes him much distress.
He has lost much if not all of his sexual drive and feels very embarrassed at not being able to perform satisfactorily. The sexual dysfunction is psychological in nature.
Psychiatric illness: He is suffering from Adjustment Disorder.
He is depressed and worried about his future. He has found it hard to adjust to his disabilities and how to relate to other people, especially his wife.
His self-esteem is low. He lacks interest in most activities and feels pessimistic and incapable to cope.

treatments_received: Operation on his spine performed 24 days after the accident
Follow-up treatment from a private doctor
Follow-up treatment from the MacLehose Medical Rehabilitation Centre
treatments_future: Individual psychotherapy (once every two weeks for ten sessions)
Regular medical check-up every three months
Annual check-up and treatment in case of complication

losses.description: Limited movement of his lower limbs including inability to stand without support; walking only with crutches and ankle-foot orthosis; cannot run or move quickly; cannot walk on slopes or climb stairs; awkward and clumsy walking.
Reduced sensation from his abdomen downwards; generally no sensation below the knee; limited sensation in thighs; unable to feel temperatures; paraesthesia in legs.

Double incontinence with bladder problems requiring diapers at night, need to go to toilet frequently and occasional incontinence; requires assistance for bowel movements with suppositories; empties bladder by straining and tapping.

losses.category: Loss of sexual function and sexual life
losses.description: Sexual ability greatly impaired; failure in 70% of attempts at intercourse; loss of sexual drive and embarrassment; has not had intercourse for over 1½ years.
Adjustment Disorder with depressed mood, low self-esteem, lack of interest in activities, pessimistic feeling and feelings of inability to cope.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Poor capability for lifting and carrying; poor capability for stooping; inability to crouch; reduction of efficiency of manual skills when required to stand; difficulty with household chores.
Embarrassment from incontinence and spasms, difficulty going out and participating in social activities without attendant; restricted mobility affecting socialisation.
Psychiatric illness: He is suffering from Adjustment Disorder.
